premiere.t: PREMIERE How Did We Discover X-rays? In a dark Würzburg lab in 1895, Wilhelm Röntgen covered a cathode tube so nothing should escape. Across the room, a cardboard screen painted to glow under light… glowed anyway. Something invisible had left the tube. He called it X — for unknown.
